text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
-For the first time the Supreme Court has imposed a fine on a defendant found guilty of buying heroin instead of sentencing the person to prison.

-Norwegian companies compete for contracts worth several billion dollars in the Emirates. Norwegian state-owned oil company Statoil has won a contract to build a billion dollar petrochemical plant in Abu Dhabi.
-As many as 30,000 reindeer in Norway's northernmost county Finnmark could starve to death. Snow and ice covering the ground make it difficult for the animals to find something to eat.

-The European Commission will study further if the proposed Nordic production and distribution deal between Danish brewer Carlsberg and beverage giant Coca-Cola complies with merger and monopoly rules. A year ago Coca-Cola broke up cooperation with Norwegian branded-goods conglomerate Orkla in both Norway and Sweden.
-Manager Arild Wegener at the Norwegian Shipping Association says it is unlikely that an international deal forbidding state support for shipyards will come about.

-Kristin Halvorsen, new leader of the Socialist Left Party, is pleased that billionaire investor Kjell Inge Roekke has shelved plans to build a luxuruous holiday house on an island near Oslo. Roekke's plans had annoyed some politicians.
